summary: Cockpit is a control center for software written with AI agents: it shows the project's own description (features and diagrams kept in .cockpit/) live, lights up what an agent is editing, and puts files, git, terminals and the agent chat beside it. A Node server per project (with a Svelte page and a GTK desktop shell around it) indexes the code, runs Claude Code through the Agent SDK and records each turn.

features.name: Live map of diagrams
features.description: Agent-written diagrams (loop, pipeline, dataflow, zones) drawn from .cockpit/, explained on hover and in a card over the map when a box is clicked, zoomable down to the code of a box, with boxes of uncommitted or in-progress code marked.

features.name: Files and git
features.description: File tree and editor (CodeMirror, vim keys, language servers) showing uncommitted changes in place, and a git tab with the branch, its PR/MR, status and a commit graph; a project tab beside them lists features, tests, out-of-date links and guardrails.

features.name: Agent chat
features.description: Runs Claude Code through the Agent SDK on the user's login: sessions, a model menu (opus by default), messages typed while it works, images pasted or dropped into the message, one send/stop button, Allow/Deny cards, context and plan-limit meters, and a self-check that sends the agent back when .cockpit/ or a guardrail no longer holds.

features.name: Turns and live lighting
features.description: Every agent request is a turn recorded with before/after snapshots in cockpit's own git store; the files it touches light up the map as it works. Claude Code sessions outside cockpit are recorded through hooks.

features.name: Terminals
features.description: Real shells in the project with command marks, readable by the agent, plus a Ctrl+K line that turns words into a command without running it.

features.name: Review mode
features.description: Check out a merge request or two branches and see changed boxes, files and git lists against the point where the branch left its target.

features.name: Guardrails
features.description: Checks (commands) and rules (with why and enforcement layer) in .cockpit/guardrails.json, run at the end of a turn that edited files; the agent is sent back for checks it broke.

features.name: Private descriptions and workspaces
features.description: A project's .cockpit/ can be kept out of its repo, per branch, and synced between machines through a private repo; workspaces let several projects know about each other.

features.name: Code index (Rust, C/C++, Zig, TypeScript)
features.description: Builds the modules and items that .cockpit/ links name: rust-analyzer or scip-clang SCIP indexes, or cockpit's own scanners for Zig and TypeScript/JavaScript (with a Rust crate beside a TypeScript project added in). The modules and check-arch commands print and check against it.
features.note: The TypeScript scanner doesn't follow tsconfig path aliases, and a quote in JSX text can confuse it for the rest of that file.

features.name: Desktop app
features.description: A GTK 4 / libadwaita window (WebKitGTK) that starts one server per project on a free port, switches projects in place, follows the desktop's accent and window buttons, and stops the servers when closed.
